title: Regression fitting, regularization and held-out assessment
outcome: Fit a small regression procedure with stable linear algebra and select regularization without using final outcomes.
key_terms: The matrix whose rows are observations and whose columns are an intercept and the predictors of a linear model.
A squared slope penalty scaled by lambda that shrinks coefficients while leaving the intercept unpenalized.
Solving ridge by stacking penalty rows under the design matrix and using QR instead of inverting normal equations.
Choosing lambda using only the development split, so the final split stays untouched until the choice is frozen.
Information from evaluation rows entering fitting or selection, which makes the reported score optimistic.
approach: `fit_ridge` checks aligned finite inputs and a nonnegative penalty, refuses an unidentified unpenalized design, then solves an augmented least-squares system with one extra row `[0, sqrt(penalty)]` that shrinks only the slope. Penalties are chosen by development error on x = 4 and 5, and the final rows x = 6 and 7 are used once afterward.

exercises.title: Recover the known model
exercises.task: Fit the exact line without a penalty.
exercises.hint: Use the authored equation as an independent reference.
exercises.answer: A correct numerical recovery validates this fixture, not a population inference.
exercises.why: Targets `1 .+ 2x` lie exactly on a line, so with zero penalty the least-squares solution is `[1, 2]` and the training error is essentially zero.
exercises.wrong: Comparing the fit to coefficients produced by the same function cannot catch an error in the augmented system.

exercises.title: Trace penalty selection
exercises.task: Compare all four development errors in case B.
exercises.hint: Use only the development labels for the choice.
exercises.answer: The final outcomes remain assessment inputs rather than selection inputs.
exercises.why: Among penalties 0, 1, 2 and 4, the development error is smallest for 2, so `argmin` selects index 3 and penalty 2.
exercises.wrong: Choosing the penalty with the lowest training error always picks 0, because the penalty only adds bias on the training rows.

exercises.title: Inspect the selected fit
exercises.task: Derive the case B intercept and slope.
exercises.hint: Use centered sums or the stated augmented system.
exercises.answer: An independent derivation checks the implementation and penalty convention.
exercises.why: Penalty 2 gives intercept 12/7 and slope 13/7, which predict 64/7 at x = 4 and 11 at x = 5, so the errors are 1/7 and 0 and the MSE is 1/98.
exercises.wrong: Penalizing the intercept as well changes both coefficients and no longer matches the augmented row `[0, sqrt(penalty)]`.
exercises.verify: Example B asserts `fits[selected] ≈ [12/7, 13/7]`; recompute the two predictions by hand.

exercises.title: Keep the final set separate
exercises.task: Alter only the final labels after selection.
exercises.expected: The chosen penalty must remain unchanged.
exercises.answer: If final labels change the selection, the procedure is leaking assessment information.
exercises.why: The selection uses only `development_errors`, so changing the final labels 13 and 15 cannot change `selected`.
exercises.wrong: Picking the penalty after looking at final error turns the final set into a second development set and biases the reported 5/98.
exercises.verify: Edit the final labels in an owned copy and confirm `penalties[selected]` is still 2.

exercises.title: Reject nonidentification
exercises.task: Fit an unpenalized design with identical predictor values.
exercises.expected: The teaching helper raises an explicit error.
exercises.hint: A coefficient interpretation requires the declared rank condition.
exercises.answer: A numerical solution selection rule should not be mistaken for scientific identification.
exercises.why: `x = [1, 1]` makes the design columns proportional, so with penalty 0 `rank(design) < 2` and the helper throws `ArgumentError`.
exercises.wrong: Letting `\` return some least-squares answer and reporting its slope pretends a slope can be estimated from one x value.

exercises.title: Report scope
exercises.task: Use two final rows to describe the model.
exercises.expected: Report the observed error without a broad accuracy guarantee.
exercises.hint: The fixture was designed for arithmetic inspection.
exercises.answer: Real deployment evidence needs representative independent data, uncertainty and diagnostics.
exercises.why: The final error 5/98 comes from two hand-built rows, so it describes this fixture and nothing about other data.
exercises.wrong: Quoting 5/98 as expected accuracy on new data treats an arithmetic exercise as a validation study.
exercises.verify: Report the final error with its row count and a statement that the rows are synthetic.

checks_note: Four `ArgumentError` cases cover a constant x column with no penalty, mismatched lengths, a negative penalty and a nonfinite input, so `fit_ridge` rejects each before solving. `predict([1, 2], [0, 1]) == [1, 3]` uses literal coefficients, and `mse([1, 2], [1, 4]) == 2` averages squared errors of 0 and 4.
